goal.text: MiHa is a reference-grade browser agent harness: its budget, its laws and its document graph are all machine-checked, and every claim below is proven with a negative control
goal.reason: The aim now covers the implementation and its budgets, not only the decision record

claims.text: Every relative document link and every ADR supersedes target in the decision record resolves to a file that exists, and the supersedes chain terminates without looping

review.reason: Owner re-read the decision: the layer diagram no longer names a protocol layer that the tree does not have, and the diagram is now checked against the tree

claims.falsifier: A document links to a file that does not exist, or an ADR names a missing or looping supersedes target
claims.control: printf '\n[missing decision](docs/adr/9999-absent.md)\n' >> README.md

claims.text: Every decision label referenced anywhere in the documentation is defined by an ADR heading, each ADR's labels are contiguous from D1, and no ADR defines decisions that nothing else references

review.reason: Owner re-read the decision: the layer diagram was corrected to match the tree, and the layer agreement is now checked by a machine

claims.falsifier: A referenced decision label has no definition, an ADR skips or repeats a label, or an ADR contains decisions that nothing else references
claims.control:
printf '
### D200. A decision nobody references

Some text.
' >> docs/adr/0002-core-harness.md

claims.text: Every measurement stated in the research documents carries a source: either a file and line, a URL, or a caption directly above the table that declares where the numbers come from

review.reason: Owner re-read the decision: the layer diagram was corrected to match the tree, and the layer agreement is now checked by a machine

claims.falsifier: A table row states a measurement with no source in the row and no source caption above its table
claims.control: sed -i '/^Source: measured on this machine against/,+3d' docs/research/02-scenario-runtime-landscape.md

claims.text: The published browser bundle, the per-layer code-line budgets, the runtime dependency count and the absence of any in the source all hold within the limits declared in ADR 0004

review.reason: ADR 0004 D19 amended again: the core ceiling is 2500 LOC, the layer table is machine-compared with the build, the arithmetic and the wording are corrected, and the refactoring's observable changes are written out; the bundle ceiling and the zero-dependency limit are unchanged

claims.falsifier: The browser bundle exceeds 30 000 B gzip, a layer exceeds its line budget, a runtime dependency is declared, or any appears in src/
claims.control: printf '\nexport const broken: any = 1;\n' >> src/core/messages.ts

claims.text: The event stream satisfies laws S1 to S7 as written in ADR 0004 D22: events arrive in push order exactly once, result resolves once with the terminal value, late events are ignored, iteration ends after the terminal event, nothing is lost between a push and the start of iteration, a failure ends iteration by throwing and rejects result, and a close without a terminal event rejects result and ends iteration

review.reason: ADR 0004 D19 amended: the layer budget table, the core ceiling and the amendment note; the stream's laws are untouched

claims.falsifier: A law is broken: order or count of delivered events changes, result resolves with the wrong value or more than once, a late event is delivered, or an event pushed before iteration is lost
claims.control: sed -i 's/this.#buffer.shift() as T/this.#buffer.pop() as T/' src/core/event-stream.ts

claims.text: The tool-parameter dialect satisfies laws C1 to C3 as written in ADR 0004 D22: every value the dialect admits is accepted, every value it does not admit is rejected with an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer path, and coercion happens only where the dialect says so. The admission set is the table in the decision, not the implementation

review.reason: ADR 0004 D19 amended: the layer budget table, the core ceiling and the amendment note; the dialect's laws are untouched

claims.falsifier: A value the dialect admits is rejected, a rejected value carries no path, or a value is coerced where the dialect did not ask for coercion
claims.control: sed -i 's/} else if (schema.coerce \&\& typeof value === "string") {/} else if (typeof value === "string") {/' src/schema/dialect.ts

claims.text: The dispatch planner satisfies laws M1, M2 and M3 and policy T1: every call of a batch appears exactly once across the plan and the rejections, a call whose arguments did not arrive complete is never planned for execution, a failed tool is a result carrying isError rather than ordinary content, and an exclusive tool runs alone while shared tools around it still share a group
claims.falsifier: A call is planned and rejected at once or neither, a call with unparseable arguments reaches a group, a failure is reported as ordinary content, or an exclusive tool shares a group with another exclusive tool
claims.control: sed -i 's/if (tool.concurrency === "exclusive") {/if (false) {/' src/core/tools.ts

claims.text: The state machine and the driver keep laws M1 to M4 and T4 over a whole run: every tool call of every batch receives exactly one result -- including on rejection, tool failure, truncation, provider error and cancellation -- the results are recorded in assistant order, a failed tool is a result carrying isError, a provider failure is an event that leaves every streamed call answered, and an aborted signal ends the run at the next boundary with every in-flight call answered
claims.falsifier: A call is left unanswered on any path, a call with unparseable arguments reaches a group, a failure becomes ordinary content or a thrown error, or the results are recorded in completion order
claims.control: sed -i 's/const flushed = flushResults(evolve(state, { results }), outputs);/const flushed = { ...state, phase: "settling" as const, results: [] };/' src/core/run.ts

claims.text: The commit gate runs every check that needs only bun — the budget, the documents and the tests — and all of them pass
claims.falsifier: One of the checks is not run by the gate, or one of them fails. The type check is deliberately not claimed: the isolated evidence copy is a git clone with no node_modules, so a control there would fail for a reason unrelated to its subject, and the method counts an infrastructure failure as no refutation at all
claims.control: sed -i 's/expect(seen).toEqual(\[\"a\", \"b\", \"z\"\]);/expect(seen).toEqual([\"WRONG\"]);/' test/event-stream.test.ts

claims.text: The provider adapter never throws and never rejects: a network failure, a refusal, a malformed chunk, a tool call without a stream index, any exception raised while reading the provider's body, and a stream that ends without a terminal event all arrive at the core as an error event, so the core's pairing invariant survives a broken provider

review.reason: ADR 0005 D32's module table refreshed to the modules that exist now; the adapter's law and its falsifier are unchanged

claims.falsifier: The adapter raises, or a stream that ends without a terminal event leaves the core waiting instead of receiving an error
claims.control: sed -i 's/if (!sawTerminal) {/if (false) {/' src/llm/openai-compat.ts

claims.text: Every fragment of a tool call's arguments reaches the core in order and attached to the right call: parallel calls are correlated by their stream index, the arguments of each call concatenate to exactly what the provider sent, a call whose id arrives late still starts once and carries every fragment, and a call without a stream index is refused rather than merged into another call

review.reason: ADR 0005 D32's module table refreshed to the modules that exist now; the arguments-intact law and its falsifier are unchanged

claims.falsifier: A fragment is lost, reordered, attached to the wrong call, or a call starts twice
claims.control: sed -i 's/this.#byIndex.get(delta.index)/this.#byIndex.get(0)/' src/llm/tool-calls.ts

claims.text: The layers named in the architectural decision are exactly the layers the source tree has, every one of them has a declared budget, and the budget numbers the quality bar states are the numbers the build enforces
claims.falsifier: The decision names a layer the tree does not have, the tree has a layer the decision does not name, a layer has no budget, or a budget number in the decision differs from the number the build enforces
claims.control: sed -i 's/| `core` | 2500 |/| `core` | 2600 |/' docs/adr/0004-quality-bar.md

claims.text: The capability bridge is a closed set: only a capability that is an **own** entry of the host's table is reachable, a name inherited from Object.prototype is not registered and is refused by name, and the caller is told which capability was refused
claims.falsifier: A capability the host did not register can be called, or the caller is not told which capability was refused
claims.control: sed -i 's/Object.hasOwn(capabilities, frame.capability)/true/' src/worker/bridge.ts

claims.text: A capability that fails rejects the caller with an Error whose message is **exactly** the failure's message: error.message for an Error, String(value) otherwise, and a capability failure and a carrying failure stay distinguishable from each other
claims.falsifier: A failing capability resolves instead of rejecting, or the caller is told something other than what failed
claims.control: sed -i 's/error: messageOf(error)/error: "the capability failed"/' src/worker/bridge.ts

claims.text: Every capability call is answered exactly once, and the answer reaches the caller that asked: two concurrent calls never receive each other's answers, and an answer whose id matches no pending call is discarded rather than given to another caller
claims.falsifier: An answer reaches the wrong caller, an answer is delivered twice, or a call is never answered
claims.control: sed -i 's/const pending = byId.get(frame.id);/const pending = byId.values().next().value;/' src/worker/bridge.ts

claims.text: A value the channel cannot carry fails the call with an error, in both directions: arguments that cannot be sent and a result that cannot be sent. Neither replaces the other, and the caller is never left waiting for an answer that cannot arrive
claims.falsifier: An argument or a result that the channel refuses leaves the caller waiting, or the failure is reported as something other than a carrying failure
claims.control: sed -i 's/"the arguments cannot be sent"/"the call failed"/' src/worker/bridge.ts

claims.text: Every capability call that reaches the host is answered exactly once: a call that succeeded, one that failed and one that was refused each produce a single answer, and no answer is sent for a call that was never made
claims.falsifier: A call receives two answers, or a call receives none
claims.control: sed -i 's/if (tryPost(port, frame)) return;/if (tryPost(port, frame)) { port.post(frame); return; }/' src/worker/bridge.ts

claims.text: The worker host hands the bridge the application's capability table and nothing else, so the set of capability names the worker can reach is exactly the set of own keys of that table. It passes every event frame it receives to onEvent, unchanged and in arrival order. After terminate() returns it posts no further frame to the worker, including an answer to a call that was in flight. It never lets an exception from the worker, a capability or the channel escape into the application's thread; an exception raised by the application's own onEvent callback is the application's, and propagates
claims.falsifier: The worker reaches a capability the host did not register, an event arrives out of order or not at all, a call that arrives after the realm ended is answered, or the host raises out of a broken worker
claims.control: sed -i -E 's/(terminate[^a-zA-Z]{0,12}\{)/& return;/' src/worker/host.ts

claims.text: The delegating side sends exactly one offer, carrying the protocol version, the task id, the task and the context, and nothing else: the delegator's tools are never reachable by the peer. It forwards every event the peer sends for that task, in arrival order, and ignores frames for another task and frames it does not know. The task resolves with the peer's outcome verbatim, a refusal resolves as a failure whose error is the peer's reason, and cancelling posts a cancel frame
claims.falsifier: The offer carries the delegator's tools, a peer's call to one of them is answered, an event arrives out of order or is dropped, a refusal loses its reason, or the outcome never resolves
claims.control: sed -i 's/finish(frame.outcome);/finish({ kind: "completed" });/' src/exchange/delegate.ts

claims.text: The driver asks the host's async approve seam before each tool runs: a denial becomes an error tool result the model reads while the tool never runs, a rewrite is re-validated and only a valid one reaches the tool, the host sees the call, the tool and the already-validated arguments, and with no seam every planned tool runs
claims.falsifier: a planned tool executing before the host answers, a denial leaving its call without exactly one error result, or an unvalidated rewrite reaching the tool
claims.control: sed -i 's/if (decision.kind === "deny") {/if (false) {/' src/core/loop.ts

claims.text: Every tool result that reaches the transcript is budgeted at one seam - a rejection, a failure, a synthetic answer and a real result alike - and so is a partial result on the live progress channel: text over the budget keeps the head and the tail halves of it and carries a block naming the bytes actually dropped and the total, the kept bytes fit the budget, an under-budget result passes verbatim, a zero budget keeps nothing but the announcement, a nonsense budget is the default, Infinity disables, non-text blocks pass through, and the default is 8192

review.reason: ADR 0009 D50 extended with the live progress channel and the transcript/event/request oracles; the implementation and the verifier were both strengthened after two discriminator rounds

claims.falsifier: a result over the budget reaching the transcript whole, a cut that loses the head or the tail or the numbers, a failure result exempt from the budget, or a host override ignored
claims.control: sed -i 's/if (totalBytes <= limit) return content;/if (true) return content;/' src/core/budget.ts

claims.text: A harness that says nothing about turns makes at most 32 provider requests and ends with limitReached naming 32; a harness that states a limit is heard in every direction - below the default, above it, and zero, which makes no provider request at all; a nonsense limit is the default

review.reason: ADR 0009 D51 extended with the nonsense-limit rule; the implementation and the verifier were strengthened after two discriminator rounds

claims.falsifier: the default missing so an unconfigured harness runs forever, or a stated limit ignored
claims.control: sed -i 's/turnLimit: resolveTurnLimit(config.turnLimit),/turnLimit: config.turnLimit ?? 999,/' src/core/run.ts

claims.text: The journal is one append-only log of durable events, every entry carrying a monotonic sequence and one version: a tool call joins the assistant message that asked for it and no other, a block is the model's answer to a refusal rather than a hole, a compaction collapses every item that began before the boundary and the answers to the calls it took with it, a change replaces the model-facing view of the entry it names - the entry it absorbed included - while the history stays untouched, the fold never rewrites the state it was given, and folding the log forward entry by entry gives the same context as projecting the whole log
claims.falsifier: a tool call joined to another assistant message, a refusal the model never sees, a compaction that leaves an answer whose question is gone, a change that rewrites the history or moves the entry it names, a fold that mutates its state, or a forward fold that differs from the projection of the whole log
claims.control: sed -i 's/entries\.reduce(foldContext, initialContextState())/entries.slice(1).reduce(foldContext, initialContextState())/' src/core/journal.ts

claims.text: The core keeps a bounded window of the journal resident - at most 64 entries, and a window of zero keeps none - while the host receives every entry with a gapless sequence and one version, even when the run is cancelled at once or the provider throws, and the last entries reach the host before the terminal event, so a consumer that closes on it keeps them. The model's context stays whole and is a budget of its own, and an answer the run holds but has not written is written when the run is cancelled, so no call is left unanswered
claims.falsifier: the resident journal growing with the length of the run, the host losing an entry or the sequence losing a number, the terminal event reaching the host before the last entries, the context losing a message, or a call left unanswered in the log
claims.control: sed -i 's/const kept = Math.max(0, state.entries.length + 1 - state.journalWindow);/const kept = 0;/' src/core/run.ts

claims.text: The core keeps the model's context within its budget: it measures the folded context in bytes, and when the context is over the budget the range that does not fit is collapsed into a digest entry, so what the provider receives fits the budget - unless the entries that follow alone exceed it, which the core cannot shrink. The journal keeps the whole history, the digest says what it swallowed, and what follows the collapse still pairs: a question and its answer

review.reason: ADR 0010 D55 and D58 refined after a second discriminator round: the digest always has room to say what it swallowed, the collapse runs after everything the turn put into the context, and a swallowed question's answer is an orphan that is not projected

claims.falsifier: what the provider receives growing past the budget, a collapse that drops the entries after the boundary, loses the history or orphans an answer, or a digest that does not say what it swallowed
claims.control: sed -i 's/if (state.context.bytes <= state.contextBudget) return state;/if (true) return state;/' src/core/run.ts

claims.text: The receiving side of the exchange runs the peer's task with its own tools and reports what happened: it refuses a task it will not take and says why, refuses a peer that speaks another version, accepts a task it takes, sends the run's journal entries back as they are written, ends the task with the run's outcome, and stops the run when the peer cancels. A peer never receives a callable handle on the receiving side's tools.

review.reason: ADR 0011 re-read after the discriminator round: the receiving side waits for its own calls before it sends the result, a throwing host is refused with a reason, a refusal without a reason is given one, a cancel before the offer withdraws the task, and the core's order (the last entries before the terminal event) is stated as the core's promise

claims.falsifier: a task accepted without the peer being told, a refusal without a reason, a foreign version accepted, the run's entries not reaching the peer, an outcome that is not the run's own, a cancelled run that keeps working, or a peer left able to call the receiving side's tools
claims.control: sed -i 's/if (!send({ kind: "accept", taskId })) return;/if (!send({ kind: "refuse", taskId, reason: "no" })) return;/' src/exchange/receive.ts

claims.text: The cassette records the provider's responses keyed by the request that asked for them, and a recorded run replays to the same journal: the replay answers the same requests with the same responses, a request the recording does not hold is reported as a divergence naming that request, and nothing but the provider's responses is recorded - the journal itself is the trace.

review.reason: ADR 0012 re-read after the discriminator round: the canonical form tags the types so a number and its name are different requests, a key holds a list so each recorded run replays to its own journal, a cassette of another version is refused, and the cassette is handed out as a snapshot

claims.falsifier: a replay that answers differently from the recording, a missing request that is answered silently, a divergence that does not name the request, or the recording holding something the journal already holds
claims.control: sed -i 's|return hash(canonical(requestForm(request)));|return "0".repeat(16);|' src/trace/cassette.ts

claims.text: MiniMax-M3's OpenAI-compatible stream reaches the core as the core's own events: the thinking as reasoning deltas, the text as text deltas, the tool calls correlated by their stream index, and the usage counted from the wire's own spelling (prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, the reasoning tokens and the cached prompt tokens) — and the adapter never raises, never rejects and never reports a stream that the provider had already finished
claims.falsifier: the fixture's thinking not reaching the core as a reasoning delta, a tool call not correlating, the usage not arriving, or the adapter raising
claims.control: sed -i 's/delta: delta.reasoning_content };/delta: "" };/' src/llm/openai-compat.ts

claims.text: The host may rewrite the provider request in flight: the driver passes the core's request through the host's prepareRequest before the provider performs it, the provider receives exactly what the seam returned, a seam that throws becomes a provider error the run reports rather than a crash, and a host without the seam changes nothing.
claims.falsifier: the provider receiving the core's request untouched while a seam is installed, the rewrite applied to the wrong request, a throwing seam taking the run down instead of becoming an error event, or a host without the seam changing what the provider receives
claims.control: sed -i 's/request = await host.prepareRequest(request, signal);/await host.prepareRequest(request, signal);/' src/core/loop.ts

claims.text: The run's phase is a function of the journal's tail and the run's ephemeral state, never a field that can disagree with them: the same journal and the same ephemeral state always name the same phase, and the phase is what the driver reads to know whether the run is over.
claims.falsifier: two states with the same journal tail and the same ephemeral state naming different phases, a phase that disagrees with the journal, or the driver's notion of 'the run is over' differing from the derived phase
claims.control: sed -i 's/if (state.turn > state.answered) return "requesting";/if (state.turn >= state.answered) return "requesting";/' src/core/run.ts

claims.text: The receiving side's decisions are taken and visible: a refusal may carry a declaration of what this side can do and the peer sees it; a transport that throws ends the task as a failure instead of leaving the peer waiting; our own tools stay transparent to the approve seam (the same name, the same dialect, the same behaviour); and the host's journal hook and the peer's event frames cannot lose an entry between them.
claims.falsifier: a declaration dropped on the way to the peer, a throwing transport leaving the outcome unsettled, the approve seam seeing a different tool than the host's own, or an entry written to the journal that the peer never hears
claims.control: sed -i 's/if (!send({ kind: "accept", taskId })) return;/if (!send({ kind: "refuse", taskId, reason: "no" })) return;/' src/exchange/receive.ts

claims.text: The interface layer turns a flat spec into a tree without running anything: a spec that names a component the registry does not have, or a property the component does not declare, is refused before the tree is built; the tree is plain data; and the same spec always produces the same tree.
claims.falsifier: a spec naming an unknown component accepted, a spec with an unknown property accepted, the tree carrying a function or a script, or the same spec producing two different trees
claims.control: sed -i 's/if (!definition.properties.includes(key)) {/if (false) {/' src/ui/tree.ts

claims.text: The registry is a closed set: a component name the registry does not have is refused, a property the component does not declare is refused, a value that is not data is refused, a patch substitutes the host's own component exactly once, and a patch may not reach outside the registry.
claims.falsifier: a name of Object.prototype resolving to a component, a spec with an unknown property accepted, a property carrying a function or a class instance, a patch applied twice, or a patch substituting a component the registry does not have
claims.control: sed -i 's/return registry.definitions.get(name);/return (registry.definitions as unknown as Record<string, ComponentDefinition>)[name] as ComponentDefinition | undefined;/' src/ui/registry.ts

claims.text: The peer's frames travel over a WebSocket: a frame that is sent arrives once and in order, a frame that arrives is delivered to every listener and to nobody else, a frame that cannot be sent is reported rather than thrown, and a closed port sends nothing and delivers nothing more.
claims.falsifier: a frame delivered twice or out of order, a listener receiving another task's frame, a broken socket throwing into the run, or a closed port still delivering
claims.control: sed -i 's/report({ error: asError(error), frame: message });/throw asError(error);/' src/exchange/websocket.ts

claims.text: A transport that reports that a frame could not be carried ends the task on both sides: the delegating side and the receiving side resolve it as a failure that says the peer could not be reached, and a run does not start on a peer that never heard the accept.
claims.falsifier: a task that waits for an answer that is not coming, or a run that starts on a peer that never heard the accept
claims.control: sed -i 's/port.onFailure?.((failure) => {/port.onFailure?.(() => {/' src/exchange/delegate.ts

claims.text: The harness runs in a browser: an example application embeds it in a worker, the agent calls the application's own tools through the bridge, a refusal asks the human and the run continues, the journal reaches the page as it is written, and the whole example bundles well inside the ceiling.
claims.falsifier: the example not bundling, the bundle over the ceiling, the agent calling a tool the page never offered, a refusal the human cannot answer, or the journal never reaching the page
claims.control: sed -i 's|append: (entry) => channel.post(journalFrame(entry)),|append: (entry) => { void entry; },|' examples/browser/worker.ts

claims.text: A tool call cannot hold the run open forever: the driver answers a call that outlives the tool timeout with an ordinary error result, tells the tool through its signal, and ignores the tool's late answer - and a call that finishes in time is untouched.
claims.falsifier: a call that outlives the timeout left unanswered, the tool's late answer producing a second answer, the tool not being told, or a call that finishes in time being disturbed
claims.control: sed -i 's/reject(new Error(`the tool did not finish within ${String(timeout)} ms`));/resolve({ content: [] });/' src/core/loop.ts

claims.text: A host that can summarize better does: when the core collapses a range, the driver asks the host for a summary of what it collapsed and applies a change, so the model reads the host's summary instead of the mechanical digest - while the journal keeps both, and a host without a summarizer, or one that fails, leaves the mechanical digest exactly as it was.
claims.falsifier: the host's summary never reaching the model, the mechanical digest being replaced by something else, the journal losing the collapsed range, or a failing summarizer breaking the run
claims.control: sed -i 's/summary = await host.summarize(collapsed, entry.summary);/summary = entry.summary;/' src/core/loop.ts
